topic.title: Upgrading Web Author from Version 28.1 to 29.0

body.p: This migration guide describes the main changes that administrators and integrators should review when upgrading Oxygen XML Web Author or Oxygen XML Web Author Component from version 28.1 to version 29.0.

The information in this topic is intended for system administrators, deployment engineers, and integrators who maintain advanced Web Author deployments, custom plug-ins, custom authentication configurations, or WAR-based installations.

section.title: Migration Overview
section.p: Version 29.0 updates several core and platform components. To avoid disrupting the live environment, first upgrade a separate test deployment, then back up the production deployment before applying the changes to it.

section.title: Apache Tomcat Upgraded from Tomcat 9 to Tomcat 10.1
section.p: Oxygen XML Web Author 29.0 and the License Servlet both require Apache Tomcat 10.1. Earlier Web Author versions used Tomcat 9, which is not compatible with Web Author 29.0.

ul.li: If you use the Oxygen XML Web Author product distribution, Tomcat 10.1 is already included and the bundled configuration files are updated accordingly.
If you deploy Oxygen XML Web Author Component or Oxygen License Servlet from the WAR distribution, deploy it on Tomcat 10.1.

section.p: Plugins may be affected if their third-party libraries depend on the javax.* API interfaces, which are no longer available at runtime in Tomcat 10. Tomcat 10 instead provides the equivalent servlet interfaces under jakarta.*.
Recommended actions:

ol.li: If you are using the WAR distribution, deploy it in Tomcat 10.1.
Review any customized Tomcat 9 configuration files and migrate them to the format used by Tomcat 10.1.

Verify that plug-ins and their third-party dependencies support the Servlet 6 runtime, which uses jakarta. interfaces instead of javax.. Pay particular attention to serialization and deserialization libraries such as Jackson or Gson, and to DTOs that rely on javax.annotation classes.
If you made custom changes to web.xml, you must migrate them because the web.xml file has changed in Web Author 29.

Review the Apache Tomcat migration documentation for additional compatibility requirements:
Apache Tomcat 10.0 Migration Guide
Apache Tomcat 10.1 Migration Guide

section.title: Apache Shiro Upgraded from Version 2.2.1 to 3.0.0
section.p: Recommended actions:

ol.li: If you customized the shiro.ini file, revalidate each change to make sure it works with Shiro 3.0.0. The default shiro.ini file has not changed between versions 28.1 and 29.0.
If you encounter problems, also review the Apache Shiro migration documentation: Migrating from Shiro 2.x to 3.x.

section.title: Secure Cookies Behind a Reverse Proxy
section.p: In Oxygen XML Web Author 29.0, Apache Shiro 3.0.0 adds the Secure attribute to a cookie only when the application itself receives the request over HTTPS. Therefore, if Web Author is exposed to browsers over HTTPS through a reverse proxy, but the proxy forwards requests to Web Author over HTTP, the session cookie is sent without the Secure attribute — even when Web Author is configured to require it.

Two options are affected when the Secure attribute is absent. If only the Use secure cookie attribute Administration page option is enabled, Web Author still works, but the session cookie is no longer restricted to HTTPS. If the force.cookies.samesite.none configuration option is enabled, browsers reject the cookie because SameSite=None requires Secure, and Web Author fails to load with the message: Cookies are disabled. Please enable cookies!

section.title: Web Author Uses Oxygen Security Manager (Java Security Manager Was Removed from Recent Java Versions)
section.p: Oxygen XML Web Author 29.0 uses the Oxygen Security Manager. The Java Security Manager has been removed from recent Java versions and is no longer compatible with Web Author 29.0.

In version 28.1, the Java Security Manager was active by default in the Oxygen XML Web Author product distribution and could be enabled manually for the Oxygen XML Web Author Component. In version 29.0, Web Author works only with the Oxygen Security Manager (it does not work with the Java Security Manager, even on a Java version that still includes it).

The Oxygen Security Manager is enabled by default in the Web Author All Platforms, Linux, and Windows distributions. In the WAR distribution and in Oxygen XML Web Author Component, which is also distributed as a WAR, it is not configured by default. You must either enable the Oxygen Security Manager manually or explicitly disable it. Otherwise, Web Author fails to start.
If you use a WAR distribution, follow the steps and recommendations below to enable the Oxygen Security Manager:

li.p: The Java platform permanently disabled the Security Manager, as specified by JEP 486 (developed by Oracle as part of the OpenJDK project). As a result, some java.security.AccessController methods are still available in the JRE but behave differently than before. For example, java.security.AccessController.doPrivileged now runs the action without applying permission restrictions. Check that your plug-ins do not rely on the previous behavior of these methods, either in their own code or through third-party libraries. For details, see .

ol.li: Check that plug-ins do not implement java.net.URLConnection.getPermission because this is no longer supported.

Make sure that no applications other than the built-in Oxygen applications run in the same Tomcat instance, because the Oxygen Security Manager can interfere with other applications running in that JVM.

li.p: Remove system properties and arguments that are specific to the Java Security Manager, such as -Djava.security.manager and Tomcat's -security argument.

ol.li: Migrate from catalina.policy to oxygen.policy. The Oxygen Security Manager requires an oxygen.policy file that specifies permissions. If you previously had additional permissions in catalina.policy, you must now add them to oxygen.policy. You can obtain this file from the All Platforms kit. Note that oxygen.policy uses internal classes from the ro.sync.security package; it does not use JRE permission classes that are deprecated for removal and are not supported.
Specify the oxygen.policy location with the -Doxygen.security.policy system property.

Add the -javaagent:./tomcat/webapps/oxygen-xml-web-author/WEB-INF/lib/oxygen-sandbox.jar JVM argument. Ensure that the application is deployed at the oxygen-xml-web-author path and that the WAR is expanded (unzipped) before starting Tomcat; otherwise, the javaagent JAR location will not exist on disk.

Verify that Web Author starts with the Oxygen Security Manager enabled by checking logs for You are running oXygen XML Web Author with security mode enabled and that no permission-related errors or warnings from custom plug-ins appear.

section.title: Deprecated Oxygen SDK APIs
section.p: As Tomcat 10 migrated to the Jakarta APIs, we deprecated the Oxygen SDK APIs that depend on javax. This change affects the WebappServlet and WebappServletFilter extensions declared in plugin.xml with <extension type="…">.

Web Author maintains compatibility with older plug-ins that use these deprecated extension classes by using internal adapters between the Jakarta Servlet and Javax Servlet APIs. However, these adapters offer only partial compatibility. For example, async responses are not supported. Therefore, although existing filters and servlets might continue to work, you should migrate away from legacy javax.servlet-based APIs.

The application logs a startup warning for each plug-in that uses the deprecated extension. For example: The 'X' plugin uses the deprecated WebappServletPluginExtension extension. Update the affected plug-in to use the replacement extension described below.
Recommended actions:

ol.li: Replace WebappServlet extensions that use ro.sync.ecss.extensions.api.webapp.plugin.WebappServletPluginExtension with ro.sync.ecss.extensions.api.webapp.plugin.ServletPluginExtension.

Replace WebappServlet extensions with role="config" that use ro.sync.ecss.extensions.api.webapp.plugin.PluginConfigExtension with ro.sync.ecss.extensions.api.webapp.plugin.ServletPluginConfigExtension.

No replacement API was added directly in the Oxygen SDK for the deprecated WebappServletFilter extension point, which uses javax.servlet.Filter. If you still need to add a filter, configure servlet filters directly in Tomcat by editing tomcat/conf/web.xml instead of using this extension point. For details, see Apache Tomcat filter configuration.

section.title: WebSphere Support
section.p: WebSphere is no longer supported in Web Author 29.0. Although Web Author could previously be run on WebSphere by using the standard WAR distribution, that deployment option has been deprecated since version 27.0.
Recommended action: Run Web Author 29.0 on Apache Tomcat 10.1 instead.

section.title: Java Runtime
section.p: The minimum required Java version for Web Author 29.0 changed from 17 to 21.

section.title: Post-Migration Validation
section.p: After upgrading, review the server logs and test both common usage scenarios and any deployment-specific customizations.
